findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow has no typestate enum or state machine; lifecycle is represented by independent fields (status String, is_validated bool, is_sent bool) that permit every combination including illegal ones like status=\"sent\" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with is_sent=false and no sent_at_epoch_ms.
findings.failure_mode: Callers construct and mutate LeaseWorkflow into impossible lifecycle states with no compile-time or runtime enforcement, violating make-illegal-states-unrepresentable.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single LeaseState enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }) with transitions enforced by the type system and smart constructors.

findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value (e.g., \"cancelled\", \"deleted\", \"sent-sent\") with no domain constraint on valid lease states.
findings.failure_mode: Callers assign invalid status strings at will, enabling state transitions that do not correspond to any defined workflow step, breaking downstream invariants that assume valid lifecycle progression.
findings.fix: Replace with a LeaseStatus enum { Pending, Validated, Sent } and a smart constructor that rejects invalid assignments. The enum itself guarantees only valid states exist.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans. Any combination is representable: both false (valid), both true (valid), is_validated=true/is_sent=false (possibly valid but unenforced), is_validated=false/is_sent=true (illogical - sent before validated).
findings.failure_mode: The two booleans encode a 4-state machine that is not a proper workflow graph. Callers can flip either flag independently, creating states that should be impossible but are silently accepted, leading to incorrect business logic and audit trail corruption.
findings.fix: Collapse both booleans into a single LeaseState enum with explicit transition variants. Use typestate: only Validated can transition to Sent; Pending cannot become Sent without Validated first. The enum variant owns all lifecycle data.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is an optional field decoupled from is_sent bool. Invalid combinations exist: is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None (sent without a timestamp), and is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(...) (timestamp set but not yet sent).
findings.failure_mode: Optional lifecycle data lives outside the state variant that owns it. Downstream code checking is_sent cannot trust sent_at_epoch_ms, and code checking sent_at_epoch_ms cannot trust is_sent. Both fields can diverge, producing silent data inconsistency.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of LeaseState enum: enum LeaseState { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. This makes it impossible to have a timestamp without being in the Sent state, and vice versa.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive representing a domain identifier. Any string, including empty, whitespace-only, or malformed strings, can be used as a lease ID.
findings.failure_mode: Callers construct LeaseWorkflow with arbitrary strings as IDs. Empty or invalid IDs pass through silently. There is no domain-level validation, no uniqueness guarantee, and no protection against collision or injection.
findings.fix: Replace with a LeaseId newtype (e.g., pub struct LeaseId(String)) with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and returns a typed error. Further guards (format, uniqueness) can be added at the boundary.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts a fully constructed LeaseWorkflow and mutates it in place without any validation at the parse boundary. The function blindly overwrites status and flags, bypassing any smart constructor validation. Raw primitives (String for status) cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly before passing them to mark_sent.
findings.failure_mode: Even if mark_sent sets status=\"sent\", the caller may have already set status to an arbitrary value, or may have set is_validated=false while is_sent=true. The boundary function performs no preconditions check, no fallible smart constructor, and no typed error return. Invalid input flows through to the domain core unchecked.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with fn try_transition_to_sent(lease: LeaseWorkflow) -> Result<LeaseWorkflow, LeaseError>. At the parse boundary, validate all invariants (is_validated must be true, status must not be final, etc.) before constructing the Sent state. Return typed LeaseError::InvalidTransition or LeaseError::AlreadySent on failure. Better yet, redesign so the enum typestate itself prevents invalid transitions at compile time.

no profiler data exists for the allocation path through mark_sent
no allocation evidence: mark_sent does String::to_string on every call creating unbounded heap allocations for status
no command evidence: no cargo check, clippy, or test output provided

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate has no tests, no benchmarks, no typestate enforcement, no typed error taxonomy, and no smart constructors. All six typestate findings are BLOCKERs that make illegal states directly representable at compile time. The struct leaks the entire lifecycle through public fields, allowing callers to bypass all workflow invariants.
